channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: ECB’s Schnabel: “More hiking is needed to get to 2%.”
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said on Wednesday that from the present perspective, further interest rate hikes are needed to bring inflation back to the central bank’s 2% target.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Bulls retain the upper hand above 1.4000 despite overbought RSI
item.description: USD/CAD climbs to fresh highs since April 2025 on Wednesday as the Canadian Dollar (CAD) faces a double blow from a stronger US Dollar (USD) and weaker Oil prices.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average rips to records on borrowed tailwinds
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) pushed into fresh record territory again on Wednesday, but the way it got there is worth a second look. The index added roughly 1% and closed near 52,200, just below the all-time high around 52,300.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Bearish near term against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan notes that MYR has underperformed since the June FOMC as higher US yields and wider US-Malaysia rate differentials weigh on the currency.

item.title: Swiss Franc hits a ten-month low as hawkish Fed bets lift the US Dollar
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) slides to its weakest level in more than ten months on Wednesday as hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) outlook boosts the US Dollar (USD). At the time of writing, USD/CHF trades around 0.8126, extending its gains for a sixth consecutive day.

item.title: Japanese Yen holds near 162 as intervention risk remains
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) registers minimal losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday amid mixed risk appetite, with global equities fluctuating between gains and losses, while investors continue to monitor developments in the Middle East.

item.title: British Pound: Oversold slide targets 1.30 area against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report the British Pound (GBP) is softer against the US Dollar (USD) but relatively resilient versus G10 peers, with declines tied to shifting Fed expectations and softening United Kingdom (UK) yields after moderating inflation and a weak service

item.title: Euro weakens for third day as Fed hike repricing eclipses German IFO improvement
item.description: EUR/USD extends its decline on Wednesday and trades around 1.1340 at the time of writing, down 0.39% on the day, as the US Dollar (USD) benefits from renewed support driven by expectations of additional monetary tightening in the United States (US).

item.title: United Kingdom: Market-friendly Burnham path – ABN AMRO
item.description: ABN AMRO economists Bill Diviney and Larissa de Barros Fritz assess the economic and market implications of UK Prime Minister Starmer’s resignation and the likely succession of Andy Burnham.

item.title: Australian Dollar stays pressured amid cooling Australian inflation
item.description: The AUD/USD pair remained under pressure, trading at 0.6890 near a three-month low on Wednesday as investors assessed Australia’s latest inflation figures and now focus on the upcoming United States (US) Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index (PCE), the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation g

item.title: Germany: Ifo survey signals tentative recovery – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Ralph Solveen notes that Germany’s Ifo Business Climate Index rose slightly in June, mainly on a better assessment of current conditions rather than expectations.

item.title: Gold weakens to a seven-month low as Fed rate-hike bets boost the US Dollar
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) falls on Wednesday, hitting a fresh seven-month low as hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations and a stronger US Dollar (USD) keep the precious metal under pressure.

item.title: Euro: Bearish bias with scope toward 1.12 against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight renewed Euro (EUR) weakness versus the Dollar (USD), driven by widening negative Eurozone–US yield spreads and a hawkish repricing of Fed expectations while European Central Bank (ECB) views stay steady.

item.title: WTI Oil nears pre-war levels below $70 as Gulf supply fears ease
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil extends its sharp decline on Wednesday, trading around $69.70, down 4.40% on the day at the time of writing and hitting its lowest level since March 2.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Hawkish RBA tone versus tech risk – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole says AUD/USD remains under pressure from the tech-led equity sell-off, given the Australian Dollar’s high correlation with semiconductor stocks. Domestically, hotter core inflation should keep Reserve Bank of Australia communication hawkish, even without further hikes.

item.title: British Pound trades lower against Japanese Yen as BoJ hawkishness lifts the Yen
item.description: GBP/JPY trades on the back foot on Wednesday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) outperforms its major peers following hawkish signals from the Bank of Japan (BoJ). At the time of writing, the cross is trading around 212.90, down 0.20%.

item.title: US Dollar: Exceptionalism without cash demand – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu observes that recent US Dollar (USD) strength reflects United States (US) exceptionalism rather than fresh cross-border buying, as underweights have already been reduced.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Yield spreads drive extended CAD slump – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note USD/CAD continues its grind higher, with the Canadian Dollar (CAD) in a near straight-line decline since early May as wider US–Canada yield spreads drive weakness.

item.title: WTI: Bearish flows face tightening backdrop – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Ryan McKay and Bart Melek highlight ongoing selling pressure in WTI Crude as CTA liquidation nears completion while high crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz keep sentiment bearish.

item.title: Euro: Range dynamics and stretched Dollar move – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts note that EUR/USD has traded mostly between 1.14 and 1.20 over the past year, with low volatility magnifying even small breakouts.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: MAS stance keeps SGD defensive – MUFG
item.description: Lloyd Chan at MUFG views Singapore Dollar (SGD) as relatively defensive versus other ASEAN currencies thanks to Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS) tight Singapore Dollar Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (S$NEER) policy, which anchors volatility and inflation expectations.

item.title: Aluminium: Deficit view intact after risk-off selloff – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey report that Aluminium led a broad metals sell-off triggered by a sharp global equity decline and a more hawkish Federal Reserve outlook.

item.title: Silver hits fresh YTD lows as hawkish Fed bets propel the US Dollar to over one-year highs
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) drops to fresh year-to-date lows on Wednesday as hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations and a stronger US Dollar (USD) keep sellers firmly in control. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $59.39, its lowest level since December 2025.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Jobs rebound expected, RBA on alert – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that Australia’s May headline CPI slowed to 4.0% year-on-year, below consensus and their own forecast, largely on softer transport and fuel costs.

item.title: Japanese Yen remains stuck near long-term lows weighed by wide Fed-BoJ rate differential
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) remains on its back foot against a stronger US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, with the USD/JPY pair approaching 40-year highs at 161.95 again. The wide differential between the Bank of Japan's (BoJ) interest rates and those of the world's major central banks is keeping the Japane

item.title: Brazilian Real: Conditional easing path for BCB – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Dan Pan expects Brazil’s central bank, Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) to deliver a more gradual easing cycle as inflation dynamics remain challenging.

item.title: Canadian Dollar dips as Fed tightening expectations, Iran tensions bolster US Dollar
item.description: USD/CAD trades higher around 1.4230 on Wednesday after earlier reaching a more-than-one-year high at 1.4239.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: BI tightening to cushion IDR against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan notes that Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) has been supported by Bank Indonesia’s proactive tightening and FX measures, but elevated US yields and domestic policy uncertainty are testing this buffer.

item.title: Gold: Slower grind higher as forecasts cut – ING
item.description: ING’s Commodities Strategist Ewa Manthey notes that Gold has sold off sharply after record highs, pressured by higher Treasury yields, a stronger Dollar and weaker ETF demand.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Resumes downside after testing Triangle breakdown zone
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) trades 0.38% lower at around 1.3150 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Wednesday. The GBP/USD pair faces intense selling pressure as the US Dollar outperforms due to hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) bets.
